supervision: Initial 24 labeled contexts for ordinary tasks; paired worlds 21. Unlabeled pool16. Test24 ordinary,27 paired. No selection/calibration label sets. Pool oracle answers only a chosen request. Final test labels never reach learning or acquisition.
model: Every nonempty teacher-consistent feature subset up to order3 is a partial deterministic mapping. Unknown projected keys allow all known labels. SS stores class-specific sums of unique full-key phase products; exact stores matching binary learned counts. Candidate consistency/filtering uses ordinary exact training bookkeeping, not SS and not evaluator truth.
acquisition: Active uses committee Gini from unique recalled labels; unknown cells contribute uniform label votes. Descending Gini, then unknown fraction, then label-blind ID hash. This ranking is not a calibrated probability. Random uses the same seed/hash order without recalls. An exhausted hypothesis family requests no further labels; actual counts are reported.
evaluation: Twelve structured task partitions, two indistinguishable initial-world tasks, two out-of-scope order4 tasks. Four phase configurations x two acquisition seeds for SS, two acquisition seeds for exact. Three methods. Pool and test are disjoint complete contexts; projected semantic keys may overlap. Evaluate only the original held-out test queries at fixed budget checkpoints.
bounds: At most six binary-inventory fields and 3-field dependencies; no rule outside this family is promised. Candidate predictions are independent partial maps; schema and maximum dependency order are designed, not learned.
controls: Exact version-space soundness unit tests; minimal-retention ablation; random acquisition; identical-world first requests; full-pool final teacher-set equality; real zero-weight memory veto; stale/tampered teacher request rejection; retained-state and teacher-label separation.
acceptance: No method must win. Freeze before final evaluation; repeat trajectories/results/model bytes. Report correct/wrong/abstained, actual teacher counts, over-abstention, candidate and memory growth, acquisition cost, and out-of-family failures. Do not open R1 inference or claim new Japanese generation/P1/S1 integration.
